To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We used microarrays to identify reproducible changes in the gene expression profiles of the brains of two knock‐out mouse models of NCLs.
the two mouse models for Batten disease, infantile and juvenile neuronal lipofuscinoses, show different patterns of gene expression changes in the brain.
we identified changes in gene expression that are reproducible and specific to Cln1‐knockout and Cln3 knockout mice, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
neuronal ceroid lipfuscinosis, a group of inherited neurodegenerative diseases of childhood.
the identification of the molecular pathways that are affected by mutations in the genes that cause the neuronal ceroid liposfuscinosis.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of neuronal ceroid lipoprotecinosis (NCD), an autosomal recessively inherited neurodegenerative disease that affects children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cln1‐/Cln3‐knocked out mouse models are useful tools in the search of new therapeutic approaches for Batten disease.
both Cln1‐/‐ and Cln2‐/‐ mice are useful models for the human infantile and juvenile forms of NCL, respectively.
the Cln3 knockout mouse model is not an adequate model for juvenile NCL, but that the Cln1 knockout model is an appropriate model for infantile NCL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cln3 and Cln1 knockout mice are not identical models for the respective human diseases, although both models are useful for the study of NCL diseases and their possible treatments.

in the Cln1‐knockout, there is a significant up‐regulation of genes involved in the ubiquitination‐proteasome pathway, whereas in the Cln3‐mutated mice, there is a down‐regulation of a number of genes involved in synaptic transmission.

the two mutations affect different sets of genes, but the common feature of the two diseases is a decrease in the expression of a large number of genes, which may be due to the same mechanism, such as a decrease in the activity of transcriptional factors or a defect in the translation of mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cln1 and Cln3 knockout mice represent two models of BATTEN DISEASE, each with a unique gene expression profile.
, despite the fact that both the Cln1‐and Cln3‐deficient mice have similar neuropathological features, there are distinct differences in the expression of genes and proteins in the two mouse models.
the gene expression profile of the knockout mouse is not a good predictor of the gene expression profile in the human patient.
